_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-invariants.json — the factory's own declaration of WHEN each ledger invariant landed IN THIS FACTORY, read by tests/ledger_boundary.py on behalf of the gates that assert those invariants. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add a key ONLY once your factory has adopted that invariant. Every key is the NAME OF THE GATE that asserts it — close_row_revision, score_gate_recorded and subject_form are the three the template currently ships — and every value is an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp: the moment the invariant landed HERE, which is the boundary at which the rule took effect. Rows at or after it are governed by the gate; rows before it are printed as 'excused:' on every run and are NEVER backfilled, because a revision recorded today for a row that predates the rule would be a falsified record rather than a repair. The value is conventionally the instant the gate and its rule were adopted — the boundary taken in the authoring run — and NOT necessarily the landing commit's own timestamp; the two can differ by minutes, and the boundary only has to separate adopted rows from excused ones, so state the instant your factory actually took. It is a FACTORY PARAMETER, not a law: a bootstrapped factory's history is its own, so a gate that hardcoded another factory's date would judge a tree it does not describe — which is why the boundary is declared here and the gate SKIPS with a stated reason when a key is absent, rather than passing silently or borrowing a foreign date. A key that is present but unreadable (not a string, not a parseable timestamp) is a gate FAILURE, not a skip: the factory declared a boundary and the gate cannot read it, and silently skipping that would hide a broken declaration behind the same output as no declaration at all.
